sequence_description: I1 direct-endpoint attack: attempt to inject authorization parameters via an unsigned OIDC request object (alg=none) and see if Keycloak accepts it for a public client. Uses two clients to satisfy multi-identity/config diversity and to detect cross-client parameter confusion.
description: [LLM-Judge] Unsigned OIDC request object (alg=none) appears to be accepted (HTTP 200), which can enable authorization parameter injection if the server honors claims from the request object without signature validation.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Unsigned OIDC request object (alg=none) appears to be accepted (HTTP 200), which can enable authorization parameter injection if the server honors claims from the request object without signature validation.

sequence_description: I1: Direct OIDC auth endpoint should reject alg=none request objects; then apply a client policy and re-test to ensure enforcement is consistent and not bypassable by semantic mismatch.
description: [LLM-Judge] OIDC authorization endpoint accepted a request object with alg=none (unsigned JWT), which should be rejected to prevent request object tampering.

sequence_description: I5: Attempt to inject expanded authorization parameters via an unsigned OIDC request object (alg=none). If accepted, attacker can exceed intended authorization constraints by tampering with request semantics.
description: [LLM-Judge] Unsigned OIDC request object (alg=none) appears to be accepted (HTTP 200), which may allow scope/parameter injection if the broker does not enforce signed request objects.
